newsitem.title: CANADA: Northland Power in Ukrainian power deal.
newsitem.headline: Northland Power in Ukrainian power deal.

text.p: Northland Power Inc has entered a C$150 million joint venture in Ukraine in a deal formalised during a visit here by Ukrainian Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko, the Canadian Press news agency reported on Sunday.

The joint venture will reduce emissions while nearly doubling the capacity of a heat and power plant in a suburb of the Ukrainian capital Kiev. Northland, based in Toronto, will design and manage the overhaul, it said.
"Signing these documents concludes two years of tough negotiations and completes the legal process to launch this joint venture," it quoted Lazarenko as saying.
Lazarenko, in Canada on a five-day visit, said earlier that Canadian and Ukrainian companies would be signing more than C$860 million in business agreements.
The Kiev plant, built in the 1950s, supplies electricity and heat to about 300,000 residents in the area, and steam to several industries, CP said.
It said Northland stated that the project was expected to take more than two years to complete.
